$comment: Reference, not copy. This file documents what each string in a locale file means and what the English site says, so a translator has the source in front of them. It is never loaded by the site: the loader in index.ts excludes it by pattern, and its shape is not a locale file's, so nothing can render it as one. English pages carry no note and no banner, because English is the page of record. The revision a translation follows is recorded in the page's frontmatter for the drift gate and is never shown to a reader, so no string here places it.

note.template.role: The second sentence of the note under the title of every translated page, naming the text that governs where the two differ; {link} is the English page of record.

note.linkText.role: The text of the link inside note.template, which is the sentence's own subject and so carries no article of its own.

note.made.role: The first sentence of the note, saying plainly how the page was made and nothing more; no placeholder.

note.corrections.role: The third sentence of the note, inviting a correction: {issue} opens the repository's new-issue form with the language and the route already in the title, {edit} opens this page's own source file on GitHub, and both are links.
note.corrections.english: If you find any issues with the text, please open an {issue} or a {edit}.

note.correctionsFull.role: The same invitation on the one-page view of the specification, which is composed from ten files and so has no single one to edit: {issue} is the only link, and the pull request comes from the edit link beside each document's title.
note.correctionsFull.english: If you find any issues with the text, please open an {issue} or a pull request from the edit link beside each document's title.

note.issueLinkText.role: The text of the {issue} link, a short noun the sentence's own verb and article carry.

note.editLinkText.role: The text of the {edit} link, which is also the whole text of the edit link beside each document's title on the one-page view, so it has to read both inside the sentence and on its own.

specBanner.template.role: The banner at the top of a translated specification document. It has to say the page is an informative translation, name and link the normative English document, and name the frozen specification line it renders. {link} is the English document.
specBanner.template.english: This is an informative translation of {link} on the frozen 1.0 line of the specification. The English document is the normative text and governs on any difference.

specBanner.fullTemplate.role: The same banner on the locale's one-page view, which renders ten documents rather than one, so the sentence is plural. {link} is the English one-page view.
specBanner.fullTemplate.english: This is an informative translation of {link} on the frozen 1.0 line of the specification. The English documents are the normative text and govern on any difference.

specBanner.linkText.role: The text of the link inside specBanner.template and specBanner.fullTemplate.

schema.required.role: The badge on a required field in the schema reference's field table, which is also that badge's title attribute. One word.

schema.pattern.role: Introduces a field's regular expression, which follows as literal source. One word or short phrase, no punctuation.

schema.sharedShape.role: The heading over a shape several sibling keys share, rendered once instead of once per sibling.
schema.sharedShape.english: Each key below takes the same shape:

schema.linkTo.role: The accessible name of a field's deep-link anchor. {name} is the field's own key and is never translated.

schema.arrayOfObjects.role: The rendered type of an array whose items are objects.

schema.arrayOfItems.role: The rendered type of an array whose items the schema does not give one type for.

schema.arrayOfStrings.role: The rendered type of an array of strings.

schema.arrayOfNumbers.role: The rendered type of an array of numbers.

schema.arrayOfBooleans.role: The rendered type of an array of booleans.

schema.arrayOfIntegers.role: The rendered type of an array of integers.

schema.arrayOfEnum.role: The rendered type of an array whose items are one of a fixed set. {values} is that set, quoted and joined by the page from the schema's own values, so it is never translated.

schema.map.role: The rendered type of an object whose keys are matched by pattern rather than named.

schema.value.role: The rendered type of a field the schema constrains no further.

chrome.skipToContent.role: The first link on every page, which a keyboard reader takes to jump the header and land on the content. Short, and a verb phrase.

chrome.source.role: The header's link to the repository, as a reader sees it. One word where the language has one.

chrome.sourceRepository.role: The accessible name of that same link, which says where it leads and names GitHub. GitHub is a product name and stays as it is.

chrome.supportedRuntimes.role: The label over the runtimes the CLI is published for, on the Quickstart and the CLI reference. The runtime names beside it are product names and are never translated.

chrome.install.role: The accessible name of the install tabs, one tab per runtime. Leji is the specification's name and stays as it is.

chrome.copyCommand.role: The button beside the selected install command, which copies it.

chrome.copyCode.role: The button on a code block the page names no command for, which copies the block.

chrome.copied.role: What either copy button is called for the moment after it has copied, so a reader using a screen reader hears that it worked. Past tense, and short.

pageKinds.normative.role: The classification eyebrow above the title of a page the specification binds: the specification documents and the JSON Schemas. {spec} is the specification line, a version token the page places and no locale translates.

pageKinds.reference.role: The eyebrow on a page describing tooling that implements the spec, where the spec is the authority. {spec} as above.

pageKinds.guide.role: The eyebrow on task-shaped instructions for adopting Leji. Non-normative.

pageKinds.background.role: The eyebrow on a page explaining why Leji is built the way it is. Non-normative.

pageKinds.governance.role: The eyebrow on a page about how the project is run, versioned, and handed on.
